table.built_by: scripts/build_sifma_table_1276.py (`--check` rebuilds it from the tracked captures)
table.content: one row per (class, settlement date), classes A to D, 2018-01 to 2027-12, 48 dates a year (one per class per calendar month); read from the 2025-07-24 capture of the workbook (2017 to 2024), the 2025-01-19 page capture (2025) and the 2026-03-06 page capture (2026 and 2027), and from nothing else
table.limits: the workbook is the file as SIFMA served it on 2025-07-24, which carries SIFMA's later corrections (its own notes: 'Updated 3/11/2021', 'Update 7/15/21 - C settle adjusted to 6/22/22', 'update 3/24/2022', 'update 10/12/2022'; the last two correct notification dates only). The dates of the years before are therefore those of the corrected file, not necessarily as first posted; no earlier capture of the workbook itself was fetched (the Mac's fetch listed the page and two workbook URLs, not the workbook URLs the earlier page captures link to, e.g. https://www.sifma.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/06/SIFMASettlementDatesCalendar.xlsx). Marked question 2 in the pull request

scheduled_availability.evidence: A settlement date is public at a decision instant only if the calendar of its year was already published at that instant, and the only evidence of when is the Internet Archive's captures of SIFMA's page (data/sifma-wayback-1276/manifest.json), which `public_from` below lists by year with the capture's timestamp (UTC, as the archive stamps it) and what in the capture shows the year's calendar. A year whose calendar no capture shows has `null`: none of its dates is public at any instant (the indicator is 0), and nothing is guessed. A year with a capture is public from the capture's instant, so a date of that year that falls before the capture is not public either (every decision that can target it was made before the capture). The block's `days: 1` and `available_time` are the earliest the registry's shape can say (a decision reads a date the business day before it at 16:00, the published records' decision time); the per-year `public_from` is the stricter, and it is the one the code applies (repo_model.sifma_mbs.public_at). The declared dates read by a decision are all later than the capture, so a calendar read at lead 2 to 5 is as public as one read at lead 1: the code applies the same per-date rule at every lead.
scheduled_availability.note: 16:00 is the published records' decision time. The captures' timestamps are the earliest instants the archive proves the calendar was public, not the instants SIFMA published it, which were earlier: the declaration is therefore conservative in the direction of not reading a date.

2018.reason: no capture shows the year's calendar. The captures of 2017-11-21 and 2018-01-15 show the page and a link to the workbook, with no label of the years it covers, and the workbook itself was not captured.

2019.reason: no capture shows the year's calendar. The capture of 2019-08-20 is labelled '(updated for 2020)', which names 2020, not 2019, and falls after most of the year's dates in any case.

2020.evidence: the page capture of 2019-08-20 (19:32:52 UTC) carries the label '(updated for 2020)' on the download of the calendar

2021.evidence: the page capture of 2020-08-14 (14:50:53 UTC) carries the label '(updated for 2021)'

2022.reason: no capture shows the year's calendar. The captures of 2021-06-17 and 2022-02-08 are labelled '(updated for 2021)'; the workbook's own note 'Update 7/15/21 - C settle adjusted to 6/22/22' shows 2022 was in the file by 15 July 2021, but that is a note inside a file captured in 2025, not an archived publication.

2023.reason: no capture shows the year's calendar. The capture of 2023-03-14 is labelled '(updated for 2024)'.

2024.evidence: the page capture of 2023-03-14 (18:44:06 UTC) carries the label '(updated for 2024)' and links the file SIFMASettlementDatesCalendarFinal2024.xlsx, uploaded under /2023/03/

2025.evidence: the page capture of 2025-01-19 (11:08:44 UTC) shows the table of the 2025 dates and the label '(updated for 2025)'. The January 2025 dates of classes A and B (1/14 and 1/16) fall before it and are not public; C and D (1/21 and 1/23) are

2026.evidence: the page capture of 2026-03-06 (15:23:32 UTC) shows the table of the 2026 and 2027 dates and 'Published on: January 29, 2026'. The date on the page is the page's own statement, not an archived instant, so the capture's timestamp is used; January and February 2026 and the first days of March are therefore not public

2027.evidence: the same capture: the table of the 2027 dates and the label '(updated for 2027)'

rule: A date `d` of class `k` is read as 1 by a decision made at instant `I` (16:00 America/New_York on the decision day) when `d` is in the table and `public_from[year(d)]` is not null and is at or before `I`; otherwise it is read as 0. A forecast of target day `T` at lead `h` is made on the decision `h` panel rows before `T`; a training pair reads the indicator of its own target row at the decision `h` rows before it. Nothing else is read: no date from a later capture, no date of a year that has none, and no stale date in place of a missing one.

coverage: agency MBS class A to D settlement dates
